_: Per-file size budgets for ui/src, and the shell rule for App.tsx, read by
scripts/gates/composition.py. THIS FILE IS THE ALLOWLIST — it is the one
source, and docs/architecture/ui.md 11.7 links here rather than restating it.
A budget is a ceiling, not a target. The gate fails when a file exceeds its
budget, and when a file over default_max_lines has no entry at all. It does
NOT fail when a count drops: ratchet the number down as the file shrinks.
.ts is in scope as well as .tsx. Capping only components would let any
component meet its cap by moving the logic into a helper beside it.
'bespoke' means a deliberate exception — the file is one cohesive thing and
splitting it would invent a boundary the behaviour does not have.
'debt' means a file that should shrink, tracked by an issue. Debt is not an
exception; it is a number that should be going down.

ui/src/App.tsx.note: Being split into feature-owned components. Was 3274, then 2323 before the file explorer moved to explorer/, then 1816 once it did, then 1815 when the terminal tab panes moved to terminal/TerminalTabPanes.tsx to pay for the graph tab, then 1813 when the left sidebar's search wrapper and tree composition moved to explorer/ExplorerPanel.tsx, which paid for the Files/Tags mode switch with two lines to spare, then 1808 when equations landed: the four repeated corePluginOn(settings.corePlugins(), ...) call sites in the Editor props collapsed to a single pluginOn helper, which also made the plugin dependency check uniform, then 1800 when the dataview runner became a toggle-derived memo in editor/dataviewWiring.ts — the shell no longer holds the signal, builds the runner or gates it in the Editor props, then 1772 when fault isolation landed: eleven FeatureBoundary wrappers and the listener group cost lines, and the hand-rolled create-note overlay paid for them by becoming the design system's ConfirmDialog, then 1756 when view freshness landed: the tab content map's prune and rename remap moved to tabs/contentCache.ts and the four per-resolver invalidate() call sites became one resolvers() group passed to editor/resolverRefresh.ts, then 1707 when the design system took over every control the shell still hand-rolled, so the markup the shell no longer owns left with them, then 1701 when the global keydown listener moved to core/globalKeys.ts, which took keyboard arbitration out of the shell and paid for both the overlay guard and clearing the toast queue on a vault switch, then 1699 when the per-action failures the shell raised directly went to the toast alongside the ones it already delegated, then 1697 when the block-ref calls moved to their own api/blocks.ts and the substrate import lost its per-name lines to the new one-line block import. Ratchet this down as each extraction lands. Completion is not a line count: it is the three extractions the ./api/ipc waiver names — document session (done), vault boot, watcher listeners. A composition root wiring this many features lands well above default_max_lines once those are out, and chasing a smaller number would mean components taking fifteen props, which is the boundary-that-does-not-exist this gate is meant to prevent.

ui/src/api/ipc.ts.note: The substrate IPC surface: vault and file operations, links, tags, rename, settings and the vault events, plus the Setting union, which is the only registry of setting keys and so stays in one piece. Was 1208 as the whole surface; each block's wire contract moved to its own module beside it (api/search.ts, api/graph.ts, api/terminal.ts and the rest) and the timed invoke to api/transport.ts, so a new block command no longer costs lines here. A new substrate command or setting key does.

ui/src/editor/Editor.tsx.note: CodeMirror host: extension assembly, the imperative EditorApi, and the anchor-scroll queue. Ratcheted 730 -> 721 when equations landed: math, equations and property-refs are all live-preview plugin flags, so livePreviewFor takes them as one LivePreviewPlugins record and the separate propertyRefsEnabled compartment and its reconfigure effect are gone. Ratcheted 721 -> 666 when the four hand-rolled resolver subscribe blocks collapsed into editor/updateSubscription.ts: the slot registers its own onCleanup, so a fifth resolver cannot repeat the leak the dataview copy had. Ratcheted 666 -> 579 when the editor core stopped naming embeds, dataview and autocomplete (#289): each block builds its own extension, facet, update subscription and DOM handler, and the core installs whatever list the shell passes, one compartment per entry.

ui/src/properties/Properties.tsx.note: The frontmatter table and its per-type cell dispatch. Raised 710 -> 711 for the data-overlay tag on the hand-rolled type menu, which is what stops a global shortcut firing through it. Self-liquidating: the menu is on the DS-migration tail (#34) and the tag leaves with it when the DS Menu takes over. Ratcheted 711 -> 709 when the date-format vocabulary moved to settings/propertyFormats.ts: the extra import it cost was paid for by folding the typeComments import onto one line.

ui/src/editor/decorations.ts.note: One Lezer tree walk producing every Live Preview decoration. Splitting by mark type would mean several walks, against the measured-performance bar. Raised 643 -> 648 when buildFor split into a timed wrapper over buildDecorations, so the walk this file exists to keep single is also the walk the perf console can see.

ui/src/ast/normalize.ts.note: Mirrors the Rust normalizer. Divergence is a correctness bug, so it stays one file that can be diffed against its counterpart.

ui/src/integrity/IntegrityPanel.tsx.note: Vault-health rows and their fetch effect. Raised 386 -> 388 for the refresh-is-not-a-load fix: one import and one tracker declaration. The cold/warm decision itself is shared in core/refreshTarget.ts rather than inlined here, so this is the whole per-panel cost.

ui/src/settings/settingsState.ts.note: The vault's persisted configuration surface: one signal, one setter and one hydrate step per setting. Length here tracks the number of settings, not tangled logic. Raised from 381 when every default moved to settings/defaults.ts — one named constant per default, so the signal initialiser and the hydrate fallback can no longer disagree, at the cost of a wrapped line each. Raised 400 -> 421 for ui.left_sidebar_mode: one signal, one setter, one hydrate step, exactly as the note describes. Raised 421 -> 423 because resetForVaultSwitch now clears corePlugins and statusbarConfig: one line each, and leaving them out is the bug in #223.

ui/src/statusbar/PendingRewrites.tsx.note: The pending-rewrites popover and its per-row apply.

ui/src/backlinks/UnlinkedMentions.tsx.note: Mention rows plus the untrack-your-own-writes fetch effect. Raised 276 -> 278 for the refresh-is-not-a-load fix: one import and one tracker declaration, the same two lines as IntegrityPanel.

ui/src/core/commands.ts.note: The command/keymap registry. It is the single source of truth for command ids, defaults and key matching (architecture/ui.md 11.2); splitting it would create a second place to register a command. Raised 260 -> 266 for graph.open: a command is six lines here and, by that same argument, has nowhere else to go.

./api/ipc.note: App still owns vault boot and the watcher listeners, which are the remaining direct IPC callers; the document session moved to core/documentSession.ts. The ban covers every module under api/ and a waiver names one exact module, so a block's own module is no way round it. The waiver goes away with vault boot and the watchers; do not add a second waiver to keep an IPC call in the shell.

./api/blocks.note: App calls createBlockRef and getBrokenBlockRefs directly for the copy-block-ref command and the statusbar's broken-ref count. They belong in a block-refs feature the shell composes, as the other extractions under this issue did.
